clue.text: Lots written about large kingdoms

indicators.note: about tells us one piece goes round the other, here round the letter for large

parts.note: reams are a great deal of writing, lots written
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A writer turns out pages and pages about vast kingdoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts REAMS around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are territories ruled by a monarch, so kingdoms in the plain synonym sense.

clue.text: Refuse to take about 100 in plane

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: in places the Roman hundred within the word for an aircraft

parts.note: a jet is a jet-engined plane
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Someone declines to bring about a hundred people aboard an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'about' is not a reversal here but the short word for concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject something is to turn it down, a straight synonym for refuse as a verb.

clue.text: A clan have dreadful downfall in the Cairngorms, perhaps

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters of the clan phrase are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A Highland clan suffers a terrible collapse in the Scottish mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges A CLAN HAVE. The Cairngorms are a mountain range in the Scottish Highlands, and 'downfall' is a fall of snow down a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a mass of snow tumbling down a mountainside, a literal downfall, and the Cairngorms are an example of where it happens.

clue.text: African statesman and staff — short stay

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a stay of execution is a delay

explanation.surface: An African leader and his aides make only a brief visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of DELAY to leave DELA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Mandela was South Africa's first black president, a famous African statesman.

clue.text: Let in old boy, very English in old hat

indicators.note: in says the first word is placed inside the string of abbreviations that follows

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A former pupil is allowed into a very English, old-fashioned club.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is the container signal; 'Let' is taken as written, and the second 'in' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old hat is out of date and no longer in use, which is exactly the meaning of a word for outmoded.

clue.text: After 'Suspicion', without question

parts.note: beyond can mean after or past, as in beyond midnight
doubt is a suspicion or misgiving

explanation.surface: Following a film called Suspicion, something is certain.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Suspicion' look like a title, perhaps the Hitchcock film, but it just means DOUBT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed past all doubt is certain, so the phrase means unquestionably.

clue.text: Regularly co-opt new dean close to busy time when the public may visit college?

definitions.text: time when the public may visit college?

indicators.note: regularly tells us to take every other letter of the hyphenated word
new signals that the letters of the following word are put in a fresh order
close to means the very end, the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A college co-opts a new dean just before a hectic period of visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes OP from CO-OPT; 'new' rearranges DEAN into ENDA; 'close to' gives Y, the last letter of BUSY.
explanation.definitionFit: An open day is a day when an institution such as a university welcomes prospective students and visitors.

clue.text: Order English knight before a court

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An English knight is ordered to appear before a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: N for knight comes from chess notation, where K is already the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a law is to decree or ordain it, so order as a verb is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Gent heading off with European band's recording

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a ring is a circular band, such as a wedding ring

explanation.surface: A man walks off as a European pop band makes a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the G from GENT to leave ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Entering data is recording it in a ledger or register, so the two verbs are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Possibly upright girl

definitions.meaning: an upright piano, called a ... in Cockney rhyming slang (... rhymes with piano in a London accent)

explanation.surface: Perhaps a well-behaved young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upright' looks like a moral quality, but it is the upright piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang uses a woman's name for the instrument, and the same name is a common forename for a woman.

clue.text: Kind and shy, like some actors are

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
to shy is to throw, and to cast is also to throw

explanation.surface: Being kind and shy is a stock personality some actors play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' is the verb to throw, not the adjective timid.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors who are always given the same sort of role are said to be stuck in one kind of part.

clue.text: Reptile that might not be what it appears to be

definitions.meaning: a lizard famous for changing colour

definitions.text: that might not be what it appears to be
definitions.meaning: a person who changes opinions or appearance to suit the company, so is not what they seem

explanation.surface: A lizard that is a master of disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: The lizard changes colour to blend in, and by extension the word describes a fickle person who shifts to suit circumstances.

clue.text: Former job with university behind protest?

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a post is a job or position
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: Someone with a former job at a university is behind a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a position marker, but it is a synonym for LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To expostulate is to remonstrate or object earnestly, so it is a way of protesting.

clue.text: Put off, in crude terms

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Someone is repelled by coarse language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters inside cruDE TERms.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage someone from acting, which is to put them off.

clue.text: Saw only deep space flicks

indicators.note: flicks suggests the letters are flicked around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone watched only films about the depths of outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flicks' looks like a noun for films, but it rearranges ONLY DEEP SPACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have clapped eyes on something is an informal idiom for having seen it.

clue.text: Cry, being cut gathering fruit

indicators.note: gathering means the first piece collects the second within it

parts.note: to shear is to cut, as sheep are sheared
a date is the fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: Someone weeps while being cut picking fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' is the container signal: the cutting word wraps round the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Shedding a tear is a common idiom for weeping, so it means to cry.

clue.text: Catholic charged, offering no resistance about being imprisoned

indicators.note: being imprisoned says the short word for about is locked inside the rest
offering no means the letter for resistance is removed

parts.note: an electric atmosphere is a charged one
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A charged Catholic offers no resistance when he is jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offering no' removes R from ELECTRIC to leave ELECTIC; 'being imprisoned' puts C inside. Catholic with a small c means broad-ranging, not the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic in its lower-case sense means wide-ranging in taste, and eclectic means drawing on many varied sources.

clue.text: Restrictive economic policy? Believe press

parts.note: to credit a story is to believe it
to squeeze is to press

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports on a tight economic policy and urges belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like journalism, but it means SQUEEZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A credit squeeze is a government restriction on lending and borrowing, a type of tight monetary policy.

clue.text: Lethargy at home I rate badly

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: badly says the following letters are poorly ordered and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stuck at home judges their own sluggishness harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges I RATE into ERTIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a lack of energy or will to act, so it is a synonym for lethargy.

clue.text: End of stage stage worker polished

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker

explanation.surface: A stagehand at the end of a show is particularly refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' takes E from the first STAGE; the second STAGE is LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant and polished both describe refined, graceful style or manners.

clue.text: Pilot admitting pressure after operation for limp

indicators.note: admitting means the first word lets the other letters in

parts.note: to pilot a plane is to fly it

indicators.note: after places the letter for pressure behind the short word for operation

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A pilot recovering from surgery is allowed a limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' is the container signal and 'after' fixes the order of the two pieces inside; 'Pilot' is the verb, not the person.
explanation.definitionFit: Floppy means hanging loosely without stiffness, which is what limp means as an adjective.

clue.text: Escape notice entering the day before

indicators.note: entering says the short word for notice goes into the other

parts.note: eve is the day before an event, as in Christmas Eve
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone slips away unnoticed by arriving the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' is the container signal; 'notice' is an advertisement, not attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or avoid, especially by cleverness.

clue.text: Farewell to the French about to go west

indicators.note: about says the French word goes round the other piece

parts.note: au is French for to the
to go west is an idiom for to die

explanation.surface: A goodbye to the French as someone sets off westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. 'about to go west' reads as leaving soon, but 'go west' is an idiom for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French goodbye, used in English as a formal farewell.

clue.text: Where one may be driven mad?

definitions.text: Where one may be driven mad?

parts.words: Where one may be driven mad?
parts.note: being driven to a place literally, versus the idiom for being made furious or crazy

explanation.surface: A question about a place where someone could be made insane.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally it is a location you are driven to; idiomatically it is a state of exasperation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of being driven to the top of a barrier means being driven to distraction or rage.

clue.text: Legendary knight's wife leaving joint in vehicle

indicators.note: in says the trimmed joint goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for wife departs from the word for a joint

parts.note: the wrist is a joint of the arm

explanation.surface: A storybook knight's wife walks out on a joint while in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes the wife's letter out of the joint, and 'in' puts what remains inside the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristram, or Tristan, is a knight of Arthurian legend, famous for his love of Isolde.

clue.text: Character in form

definitions.meaning: the composition or structure of something

explanation.surface: A personality that is on top form.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's make-up is their character, and the make-up of a thing is its constitution or form.

clue.text: Champion's card sure to be corrected

indicators.note: to be corrected says the letters are put right by reordering them

explanation.surface: A champion's playing card is sure to be marked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be corrected' rearranges CARD SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is a campaigner for a cause, and to champion a cause is to campaign for it.

clue.text: Read about brewer's last stout?

indicators.note: about says the word for read goes round the final letter

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the brewer

explanation.surface: Someone reads up on a brewer's final strong dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' gives R, the end of BREWER; 'about' puts STUDY round it. 'stout' looks like beer but is the adjective strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy and stout both describe someone strongly built and robust.
